name: page-and-api
title: Page + API
description: A landing page and the endpoint its form posts to, in one deploy — the pages are files the platform serves, the answer comes from a handler beside them, and there is one hostname, no CORS and one thing to roll back.
post_deploy:
Your site is live at {{url}}

Open it and price a run of cards. The page is a file this deploy carried; the
price comes back from the handler in the same deploy, at the same address.

Then:
  1. The pages are in public/. Edit index.html, deploy again — that is the whole
     editing story, and there is no build step.
  2. The rates are in src/pricing.js, and the page does not know them. Change one
     and every visitor is quoted the new figure on the next deploy.
  3. The pages and the handler go up as one Version, so `npx wawesome version
     switch` takes both back together. There is no second vendor to keep in step.
  4. Want your own address on it? Attach a domain from the dashboard.

On your App's own hostname the platform serves public/index.html straight from
storage, and your handler runs only for the form's POST and for addresses no
page claims. On the development path form (/x/...) every request reaches the
handler instead, which is why src/index.js keeps a short map of the pages this
deploy carries and hands them back by name.
